MAINTRA

Rethink everything.Keep the roots.

How Maintra got from its first version to 2.0. What bothered me, where I looked for inspiration, which ideas didn't survive, and what the new design language is made of.

01 The start

Three Maintras
before 2.0

Maintra exists because I kept forgetting which oil I'd put in my VW Jetta, how much, and when. Spreadsheets, paper receipts and GPT chats kept getting lost too. Then the app grew feature by feature, and every new feature claimed its own spot on the screen.

First version
1.5
1.6, before the redesign

Users said it straight: too busy, and it looks like AI slop. That was the starting point.

02 What had to stay

Six rules
before the first sketch

01

The car's history at the centre

The service timeline is the app. New features must not push it off the screen.

02

A garage, not a notebook

The car's photo hangs on the wall, yellow masking tape, stickers on boxes of parts.

03

The polaroid stays

The first 1000+ users got their own frame. It couldn't just be thrown away.

04

Answers, not buttons

A dense screen of numbers beats a screen of buttons and pictures.

05

Throw nothing away

Every existing feature stays. What you need often is one tap away.

06

Your screen, your way

You decide what goes on your screens: which blocks sit under the polaroid, what's in the corner, which frame.

03 Where the inspiration came from

Games, studios
and a real garage

I collected moodboards and looked at games and interfaces I love. I took the feel of a genre, not any one game. Below are the first sketches and trial runs that came out of it. Raw, as they were, no polish.

Gran Turismo · Forza · Need for Speed · DiRT · WRC

Racing games

  • The garage as a collection: every car has its own page, class and condition.
  • Condition by system: engine, brakes, tyres, fluids, body.
  • Calm menus where every action feels as good as a mechanical click.
Embark Studios · ARC Raiders · The Finals

Industrial UI

  • A narrow typeface for names and numbers, like on signs and labels.
  • Cut corners instead of rounded ones.
  • A dark background and one bright colour that means “press here”.
Apple HIG · iOS 26 Liquid Glass

A native feel

  • Frosted glass for panels that float over the content.
  • One or two typefaces, a clear hierarchy, big tap targets.
  • Dark and light themes from day one.
My own garage · Pajero 2008

A real garage

  • The wallpaper of small tools was already in the app. It stayed, because it's become Maintra's recognisable background.
  • The polaroid was there too. Now it holds only the photo, the mileage and the next job. You can pick the frame: classic, charcoal, the doodle for the first 1000 users, plus the frames already in the app. More will keep coming.
  • Icons from a single sheet for the whole app: straight lines, octagons, cut corners.
  • A 3D model of every car is close to impossible: thousands of models, years, trims and tuning jobs. So the centre of it all is a real photo of your own car.

What didn't survive: rankings against other owners, collectible cards, hexagons and the big HUD. What stayed from games: the car's class and condition, the menu strip, yellow as the main action.

05 Design language

A cut, an octagon
and yellow for action

I started with Barlow, the same typeface ARC Raiders uses. Then I moved to Tektur: its cut corners match the cards, buttons and icons. Fira Sans for text. Status dots became octagons instead of circles. Yellow only where you need to tap or look first.

06 Motion

Calm,
until it's time

Animation here is part of the language, not decoration. It shows where a thing came from and where it went: the polaroid becomes the header, cards slide out from under your finger, a stamp lands when a job is done. Everything is under 320 ms, except the Moment.

Calm by default

Up to 320 ms. Arrives fast, leaves faster.

Nearest the finger first

Menus open from the bottom up, 40 ms apart.

From the edge, not thin air

Cards slide in from the right and never just fade in on the spot.

Loud only in the Moment

Bounce, scale and haptics only when you finish a job.

With “Reduce motion” turned on in the system, everything is the same but without movement: simple fades or an instant change.

07 Logo

From mandala
to stroke

The name is made of maintenance and tracker, and it sounds like “mantra”. Hence the old gear with a mandala inside. It didn't fit the new language: a round, detailed mark among cut shapes. I tried everything: gears, odometers, game badges, garage rituals. It cost more than one sleepless night, and when I did sleep, I dreamed of logos.

Two letters

M and t at once: maintenance tracker in one mark.

A spring

The slanted strokes read as a shock absorber's spring. It's about the car, not an abstraction.

Room to move

The strokes can compress and rebound like suspension over a pothole. A ready-made animation for launch, sync and loading.

The 2.0 language

The same slanted lines and cuts as the buttons, cards, icons and the Tektur typeface.

08 Before and after

1.6 vs 2.0

Same data, same Pajero. The difference is that the screen now answers a question instead of listing everything.

→

The polaroid is bigger, with one number under it: how long until the oil change. Then only what's most urgent. Wishlist, documents, tyres and the shelf moved to a strip at the bottom.

→

Jobs are grouped by visit to the shop, with a total for each visit. Work done and parts bought for the shelf are kept apart.

→

Overdue, soon and later. Every row says when and why. Fewer icons and less text, calmer colours, more room to breathe.

09 Where we got to

Maintra 2.0

Dark and light themes, a classic garage view, phone and tablet, an offline map with trip stats, a vault for documents, tyres. The store screenshots are already done in twelve languages.

10 Make it yours

Dark, light
or like your phone

You pick the theme in your profile: dark, light or system. The rules stay the same, only the light changes. The garage can switch too: a polaroid with a photo, or a classic list of cards. Then come our own themes, below.

Garage
Plan
Costs
Classic garage

Themes to choose from

Three free and four in Pro. A theme changes only the background and the accent. Text, icons and statuses stay put: red is overdue, amber is soon, green is all good. You can try any of them on for a minute, and Red light can switch itself on after sunset.
